newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Texas Pacific taps banks for Del Monte LBO.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Texas Pacific taps banks for Del Monte LBO.

text.p: NEW YORK, March 4 (LPC) - BankAmerica Corp and Bankers Trust New York Corp this week will launch syndication of a $700 million loan for Texas Pacific Group's leveraged buyout of Del Monte Foods, banking sources said.
The buyout totals more than $800 million, they said.

In conjunction with the bank deal, which is the latest example of the "one-stop shopping" technique that is being heavily emphasized in the syndicated loan market, BT Securities is leading and BancAmerica Securities is co-managing a $215 million subordinated note offering, according to lenders.

One-stop shopping refers to the practice of one -- or two, in this case -- financial institution leading several or all facets of a merger or acquisition transaction, from bank financing to high-yield bond issuance to advisory services.
The loan structure includes a revolving credit and an amortizing term loan, as well as "B," "C" and "D" term loans, sources added.
The B, C and D tranches are longer-term, delayed-amortization loans marketed mostly to institutional investors such as prime rate funds and insurance companies, they said.

These so-called "institutional" tranches are one of the most important segments of the syndicated leveraged loan market because of the estimated $25 billion to $35 billion in cash that the public prime rate funds have to invest, bankers have said.
The BankAmerica and Bankers Trust loan facility, which replaces a $400 million revolver Bank of America put in place in 1996, also will be used for working capital, bankers said.
Syndication was expected to close by the end of March.
